name: In-Shader Neural Volume Ray Marching
definition: A ray marching technique where the neural network (MLP) is evaluated directly inside the CUDA kernel for each sample point, rather than pre-decoding the volume into a 3D texture or using sample-streaming. It supports multiple shading modes including gradient shading and single-shade heuristics.
summary: In-Shader Neural Volume Ray Marching evaluates neural networks directly within CUDA kernels during ray marching, enabling real-time interactive visualization of neural radiance fields without pre-decoding volumes into textures.
